subject: English
source: National Curriculum / EYFS (systematic synthetic phonics, Letters and Sounds-style sequence); no Reception material in the Drive English folder

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Listening, rhyme and first sounds
lessons.title: Bismillah and our listening walk
objectives: Listen carefully to sounds around us
Join in with bismillah and a counting rhyme

keywords.def: use your ears to notice sounds
a big sound
a small, soft sound

starter: Show me your listening ears - touch them!
Say your name in a quiet voice, then a loud voice.
Clap the beats in your name.

teach.heading: Bismillah and good listening
teach.note: Say ‘Bismillah’ together slowly. Show the class rules with actions: eyes looking, ears open, hands still. Praise children who model it. Keep to 2 minutes.

teach.heading: Sound detectives
bullets: Guess the sound: bell, clap, rain
teach.note: Hide a bell, a shaker and a pencil tap behind a screen or off camera. Play one at a time and let children guess. Accept any sensible answer and model the sentence ‘I heard a bell’.

teach.heading: Loud and quiet
bullets: Match the sound to the picture
teach.note: Show two pictures: a lion roaring and a mouse. Ask children to make the sound at the right volume. Check they can control their voices; this prepares them for oral blending later.

teach.heading: A noisy morning story
bullets: Wake up! Brrring goes the clock
teach.note: Tell the short story with sound effects. Children join in with each sound. Ask: ‘What was the first sound? What was the last?’ Do not worry about letters today; this is Phase 1 listening.

practice: I will tap the drum. Tell me: was it loud or quiet?
Close your eyes. What can you hear in the room?
Listen to the three sounds and put up one, two or three fingers for how many you heard
Make a sound with something near you for others to guess
independent: Draw something that makes a sound and say its sound to your teacher
Play ‘I heard…’ with a partner: describe one sound at home
exit: Tell me one sound you heard today. Was it loud or quiet?
lessons.homework: Listen for two sounds at home and tell a grown-up what you heard.
lessons.send: SEND: use visual cards for each sound and allow pointing to answer. EAL: pair home-language words with English. Stretch: sequence three sounds in order.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Listening, rhyme and first sounds
lessons.title: Rhyme time
objectives: Join in with nursery rhymes and songs
Hear and say words that rhyme

keywords.def: words that end with the same sound, like cat and hat
the beat of a song or poem

starter: Clap your name again. How many claps?
Which sound is louder: a drum or a whisper?
Say bismillah with me.

teach.heading: Say the rhyme together
bullets: Clap the beat as we say it
teach.note: Recite ‘Twinkle, twinkle, little star’ with actions. Repeat three times, each time a bit faster or softer. The aim is confident joining-in and a feel for rhythm.

teach.heading: What is a rhyme?
bullets: Rhyming words sound the same at the end
teach.note: Say the pairs slowly, stressing the ending. Ask ‘Do these sound the same at the end?’ Common error: children think words that start the same (bat, ball) rhyme. Gently clarify it is the ENDING.

teach.heading: Rhyme or not?
bullets: Thumb down if they do not
dog - log, sun - bun, pig - cup
teach.note: Say each pair and let children show thumbs up or down. For thumbs down, model ‘pig and cup do not rhyme’. Revisit any pair children get wrong.

teach.heading: Finish the rhyme
bullets: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall
teach.note: Say the rhyme and stop before the last word so children supply the rhyming word. Ask them to name the two words that rhyme (wall, fall).

practice: Let’s say Twinkle, Twinkle together with actions.
Do these rhyme: cat and mat?
Do these rhyme: dog and sun?
Say a word that rhymes with cat
Choose from two pictures which one rhymes with log: dog or pen
independent: Sort picture cards into ‘rhymes with hen’ and ‘does not rhyme with hen’ (pen, ten, cat, sun)
Make up a silly rhyme with a partner: ‘The cat sat on the…’
exit: Do bed and red rhyme? Tell me yes or no.
lessons.homework: Say a nursery rhyme to someone at home and clap the beat.
lessons.send: SEND: use picture cards and sing the rhyme. EAL: rhymes from home language welcome. Stretch: give three words that rhyme with ‘sun’.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Listening, rhyme and first sounds
lessons.title: First sounds and oral blending
objectives: Hear the first sound in a word
Blend sounds said by the teacher into a word (robot talk)

keywords.def: what we hear at the start of a word, like sss
push sounds together to make a word

starter: Tell me a word that rhymes with ‘bat’.
Clap the beats in ‘banana’.
What sound do you hear at the start of ‘sun’?

teach.heading: Listening for the first sound
teach.note: Use pure sounds: ‘sss’ not ‘suh’, ‘mmm’ not ‘muh’. Say the word, then stretch the first sound. Ask children to copy the first sound. Pure sounds make blending possible later.

teach.heading: I spy game
bullets: I spy with my little eye
Is it a sock? a sun?
teach.note: Place 4-5 objects near the camera: sock, sun picture, sandwich, pen. Play I spy using sounds, not letter names. Children point or name. Celebrate the correct first-sound match.

teach.heading: Robot talk
teach.note: Say sounds with a robot voice and tiny pauses, then say the whole word. Children copy. Start with 3-sound words with no tricky sounds: c-a-t, d-o-g, s-u-n. Do the same with arm blending along the arm.

teach.heading: Your turn to blend
teach.note: Say each robot word and children say the whole word. If they struggle, tap each sound on your arm and sweep. Keep the pace snappy; it should feel like a game.

practice: Say bismillah and tap the rhythm.
Which word starts with sss: sun or dog?
Clap three beats.
Say the first sound of: sun, mat, pen
Blend the robot words: d-o-g, p-i-g, s-u-n
independent: Find three things near you and say the first sound of each
Play robot talk with a partner: one says sounds, one says the word
exit: What word do the robot sounds make? m-a-p
lessons.homework: Play I spy with sounds at home with a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: use object-based blending with real items. EAL: accept names in home language for first sounds. Stretch: say the last sound too.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Letters s and a
objectives: Say the sounds s and a when shown the letters
Start to form the letters s and a

keywords.def: a shape we use to write a sound
what we say when we see a letter

starter: Robot talk: t-o-p. What is the word?
What is the first sound in ‘sun’?
Say a word that rhymes with ‘cat’.

teach.heading: The sound s
teach.note: Show s clearly. Say sss with no vowel after it. Children copy, then do a snake wiggle. Link to words: sun, sock, sandwich.

teach.heading: Writing s
teach.note: Model on a whiteboard on camera: start at the top, curl left then right. Children air-write, then write on paper or a whiteboard. Check pencil grip and sitting position.

teach.heading: The sound a
bullets: Say the short sound: a (as in ant)
teach.note: The short sound as in ant, apple. Common error: children say the letter name ‘ay’. Say ‘We say the sound a’ and use an apple picture.

teach.heading: Writing a
teach.note: Model forming a with a round shape then a straight down stroke. Many children draw the stick first or the wrong direction; slow modelling helps.

practice: Say the first sound in the pictures: sun, sock, ant, apple
Which words start with s? sun, pig, sock
Point to s and say its sound when I show cards s and a
Air-write s and a on the table with your finger
independent: Write a line of s and a on your whiteboard
Draw one thing that starts with s and one that starts with a, and say the sounds
exit: Show me the letter that says sss. Show me the letter that says a.
lessons.homework: Find something that starts with s at home and say its first sound.
lessons.send: SEND: trace letters in sand or salt tray. EAL: link sounds to picture cards. Stretch: write s and a in a word, like as.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Letters t and p
objectives: Say the sounds t and p
Form the letters t and p
Read and say simple sound-talk words

keywords.def: the sound at the start of tap
the sound at the start of pat

starter: Show me s. Show me a.
Blend: s-a-t? (It is a new word - listen first!)
Say ‘as’ in robot voice: a-s.

teach.heading: The sound t
bullets: Tap your teeth with your tongue
teach.note: Say t as a short sound without a vowel after it - ‘t’ not ‘tuh’. Use a tapping action. Show pictures: tap, tin, tent.

teach.heading: Writing t
bullets: Make a cross like a plus sign
teach.note: Model on screen. Children air-write and write. Common error: starting at the cross. Say it is a long line first, then a short cross-bar.

teach.heading: The sound p
bullets: Say a puff of air: p
Hold your hand near your mouth
teach.note: Have children hold a hand or tissue near mouth to feel the puff. Pictures: pen, pig, pan. Again no vowel: ‘p’ not ‘puh’.

teach.heading: Writing p
teach.note: Model: straight line down, go back up, then round. Remind them it hangs below the line. Practise the letters s a t p in a row on whiteboards.

practice: Show me the sound s. Show me the sound a.
First sound: sun - sss, apple - a
Say the robot word: s-a-t - sat!
Sound-talk and say the whole word: t-a-p, p-a-t, s-a-p
Spot the letter: hold up t when I say tap, p when I say pan
independent: Write t and p three times each
Find a picture starting with t or p and write the first letter
exit: What is the sound at the start of tap? What is at the start of pig?
lessons.homework: Look for the letters t and p on signs or boxes at home.
lessons.send: SEND: use tactile letters, trace in sand. EAL: name objects in home language and English. Stretch: write tap or sat.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Blending s a t p words
objectives: Blend sounds to read simple words
Read words: at, as, sat, pat, tap, sap

keywords.def: say the sounds in a word and push them together
letters that make a meaning

starter: Show me s, a, t, p. Say each sound.
Write the letter t in the air.
Robot talk: s-a-t.

teach.heading: Sound, sound, blend
bullets: Look at the letters: s a t
Sound them out: s - a - t
teach.note: Point under each letter, say its sound, then sweep under the whole word and say it. Children copy. Keep a steady, brisk rhythm.

teach.heading: More words
teach.note: Show each word and let children blend. Read ‘at’ first (2 sounds), then 3-sound words. If a child gives the wrong word, say the sounds again with them rather than guessing.

teach.heading: What does it mean?
teach.note: Link each word to meaning: act it out. Ask ‘Show me pat.’ Reading is understanding as well as decoding.

teach.heading: Spot the real word
teach.note: Introduce the idea of ‘alien’ words: nonsense words such as sab. Children blend and say whether it is a real or alien word. Good practice for decoding.

practice: Sound talk: p-a-t. What is the word?
Show me the sound t. Show me p.
What sound starts ‘sun’?
Read the words on cards: at, sat, pat
Read as, sap, tap
independent: Match word cards to pictures: tap, sap (tree sap), pat (dog)
Read a caption with your partner: a tap
exit: Read this word: tap. Now read: sat.
lessons.homework: Read the words sat, pat and tap to someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND: reduce to 3 words and use pointing. EAL: act out each word. Stretch: read alien words quickly.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Letters i and n
objectives: Say and write the sounds i and n
Blend and read words with i and n

keywords.def: the sound at the start of ink
the sound at the start of nap

starter: Read: sat, pat, tap.
Show me the letters s a t p.
Blend: s-a-p.

teach.heading: The sound i
bullets: Short sound: i as in ink
teach.note: The short i as in igloo, insect. Do not say the letter name ‘eye’. Pictures: ink, insect, igloo.

teach.heading: Writing i
teach.note: Model: a short stick down then the dot on top. Common error: placing the dot too far from the stick. Practise on the whiteboard.

teach.heading: The sound n
teach.note: Say ‘nnn’ and ask children to feel their nose. Pictures: net, nest, nut. Avoid saying ‘nuh’.

teach.heading: Writing n
teach.note: Model: a down stroke, retrace up, arch over and down. Common error: making an ‘m’ or starting with a loop. Check each child’s letter on camera.

practice: Read the words: at, sat, tap
What sound does this letter make? (show s, a, t, p)
Say the sounds when I show: i, n, t, p
Read: in, pin, tin, sit
independent: Write i and n three times each
Blend and read: pin, tin, nap
exit: What sound does i make? What sound does n make?
lessons.homework: Find the letters i and n at home and say their sounds.
lessons.send: SEND: use letter tiles. EAL: highlight vowel sounds. Stretch: write in or it.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Letters m and d
objectives: Say and write the sounds m and d
Read words: mat, map, dad, din

keywords.def: the sound at the start of mum
the sound at the start of dog

starter: Read: in, pin, tin, sit.
Say the sounds: i n s a t p.
Blend: p-i-n.

teach.heading: The sound m
teach.note: Say mmm with lips closed. Pictures: mat, moon, mug. Remind children not to add a vowel: ‘mmm’ not ‘muh’.

teach.heading: Writing m
teach.note: Model two humps. Many children make just one or three humps. Say ‘down, up and over, up and over’.

teach.heading: The sound d
teach.note: Pictures: dog, door, duck. d is often reversed with b, so teach: round first (like a), then a tall stick.

teach.heading: Writing d
teach.note: Model slowly; the round part comes first. Reversal with b is common - give frequent practice, and use a reference card on the desk.

practice: Read: tin, pin, sit.
What sound is this letter? (i, n, m, d)
Read words on screen: mat, map, dad, din
Sound out: m-a-t, d-a-d
independent: Write m and d, then write the word mat
Draw a map and label it with m
exit: What is the sound at the start of mum? And dog?
lessons.homework: Look for m and d on food packets at home.
lessons.send: SEND: use sky-writing and tracing. EAL: say mum/dad pictures in home language and English. Stretch: write dad.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Reading words with s a t p i n m d
objectives: Read CVC words with the new sounds
Spot the odd one out in a set of words

keywords.def: a word with a consonant, vowel and consonant, like sat

starter: Say each sound: s a t p i n m d
Blend: m-a-p
Is ‘tid’ a real word or alien word?

teach.heading: Read a word list
teach.note: Show each word and children sound-talk and blend. Look for fluent blending. Keep the tempo brisk. If a child stalls, return to sounding it out together.

teach.heading: Real or alien?
teach.note: Alien words test decoding without guessing. Remind children that alien words have no meaning but we can still read them.

teach.heading: Words in a sentence
teach.note: Show a short caption with a full stop. Children read it by blending, then reread more smoothly. Explain a full stop means stop.

teach.heading: Make a word
teach.note: Use letter cards or magnetic letters: model building ‘tin’ then changing to ‘pin’. Ask what changed. Introduces phoneme manipulation.

practice: Read: sat, pin, mad.
Show me the sounds: m d i n.
Blend: t-i-p.
Read each word and match to the picture: tin, map, pin, sit
Choose the real word: nap or nip? tid or tip?
independent: Build three words with letter cards and read them to a partner
Read a caption: Dad sat. A tin.
exit: Read these words: dim, nap, tip.
lessons.homework: Read the words dim, nap, tip to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND: smaller word set with pictures. EAL: demonstrate word meanings. Stretch: write each word in a sentence.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Letters and sounds - s a t p i n m d
lessons.title: Writing words and captions
objectives: Segment a word into its sounds to spell it
Write a simple word and a caption

keywords.def: break a word into its sounds
a short label that goes with a picture

starter: Blend: m-a-t, t-i-n, d-i-p
Show me how to hold a pencil.
Write the letter m in the air.

teach.heading: Say it, then write it
bullets: Sound it out: p - i - n
Write a letter for each sound
teach.note: Model segmenting using fingers: one finger per sound, then write each letter. This is the key link between reading and writing.

teach.heading: Writing a word
teach.note: Model writing ‘tin’ on camera, saying each sound as you write it. Children copy and then write ‘map’ independently. Check for correct letter orientation and size.

teach.heading: Writing a caption
teach.note: Introduce capital letters and full stops for the first time. Show: ‘A tin.’ with a capital A and a full stop. Children say ‘A tin’, then write it. Support: tracing.

teach.heading: Check your writing
bullets: Do the letters sit on the line?
Did you use a full stop?
teach.note: Teach children to point and read back what they wrote. Reading it back catches missing sounds. Praise effort and correct formation, not neatness alone.

practice: Say bismillah. Show me your pencil hold.
Segment: pin - how many sounds?
Write the letter d in the air.
Segment and write: sit, nap, mad
Write a caption for the picture: A pan.
independent: Choose three picture cards and write a caption for each
Read your captions to a partner
exit: Write the word pin. How many sounds are there?
lessons.homework: Draw a picture and write a caption using sounds you know, like ‘A map.’
lessons.send: SEND: scribe or use letter cards. EAL: say the sounds aloud in English. Stretch: write a two-word caption.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Letters g o c k and tricky words
lessons.title: Letters g and o
objectives: Say and write the sounds g and o
Read words: got, dog, pot, mop

keywords.def: the sound at the start of goat
the sound at the start of orange

starter: Read: mat, tin, dad, sip
Say the sounds: m d i n s a t p
Segment: map - how many sounds?

teach.heading: The sound g
bullets: Say a short ‘g’ at the back of the mouth
teach.note: Say g without a vowel. Children feel the sound at the back of the throat. Show goat and gate pictures. Check they do not say ‘guh’.

teach.heading: Writing g
teach.note: Model: round first (like a), then a straight line down with a tail curling left. Common error: forming a ‘9’ shape or skipping the tail. Remind them it hangs below the line.

teach.heading: The sound o
teach.note: The short o as in orange, octopus, not the letter name ‘oh’. Mouth shape round and open.

teach.heading: Writing o
teach.note: Model: start at the top and go all the way round to the left. Many children start at the bottom. Practise a line of o’s on a whiteboard.

practice: Say the sounds g and o when I show the cards
Sound-talk and blend: g-o-t, d-o-g, p-o-t
Read: got, dog, pot
Choose the picture that matches: dog or pig
independent: Write g and o in a line, then write dog
Draw a dog and write a caption: A dog.
exit: What sound does g make? What sound does o make?
Read the word got.
lessons.homework: Find the letters g and o on packaging at home and say their sounds.
lessons.send: SEND: use tracing and tactile letters. EAL: practise o and g with picture cards. Stretch: write got in a sentence.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Letters g o c k and tricky words
lessons.title: Letters c and k
objectives: Say and write the sounds c and k
Read words: cat, cap, kid, kit

keywords.def: the sound at the start of cat
the sound at the start of kit

starter: Read: got, dog, pot
Say the sounds: g o s a t p
Blend: c-a-t

teach.heading: The sound c
bullets: Say a short ‘c’ like a cough
teach.note: c and k make the same sound /k/. Say it crisply with no vowel. Pictures: cat, cap, cup. Say ‘c is for cat’ but the sound is just /k/.

teach.heading: Writing c
bullets: Leave it open like a mouth
teach.note: Model: curl round anticlockwise, open at the right. Common error: closing it into an o. Show the difference between c and o.

teach.heading: The sound k
teach.note: Explain that k makes the same sound, spelled differently. Children say the sound for both. Tell them there are more ways to spell /k/ and they will learn them.

teach.heading: Writing k
teach.note: Model: a tall straight line, then the arm and leg. Children air-write ‘Kick, kick’ with a foot movement. Check on camera.

practice: Show me the letter c. Show me k.
Blend: c-a-p, k-i-t, c-o-t
Read: cat, cap, kid
Choose real or alien word: cip, kit
independent: Write c and k three times, then write cat or kit
Match word cards to pictures: cap, kid, cot
exit: Which two letters make the sound /k/?
Read the word kit.
lessons.homework: Look for c or k at home on cereal boxes and say the sound.
lessons.send: SEND: use hand-over-hand formation if needed. EAL: link words to pictures. Stretch: write a caption: A kid.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Letters g o c k and tricky words
lessons.title: Reading and writing with g o c k
objectives: Read CVC words with all sounds learned so far
Write simple words with the sounds we know

keywords.def: a short word with a consonant, a vowel and a consonant

starter: Read: cat, kit, got, dog
Say the sounds: s a t p i n m d g o c k
Segment: cup - how many sounds?

teach.heading: Sound it, blend it
teach.note: Display words one at a time. Children sound-talk and blend. Rotate through quickly: aim for automatic recall of sounds.

teach.heading: Which word?
bullets: Is it a cat or a cot?
Is it a dog or a dig?
teach.note: Contrast pairs help children focus on the middle sound. Say each word and show pictures. Ask them to choose the picture then read the word.

teach.heading: Write a word
bullets: Write a letter for each sound
teach.note: Model segmenting and writing ‘dog’ then ask children to write ‘cap’ and ‘kid’. Check formation and left-to-right direction.

teach.heading: Write a caption
teach.note: Show the captions on the board. Highlight capital A and the full stop. Children read, then write one of their own.

practice: Read the words and match to pictures: cat, dog, kid, pot
Sound-talk and write one word as I say it: cap
Write captions for three pictures: cat, dog, pig
Read your captions aloud
independent: Make three new words with letter cards from c, a, t, p, i, n, o, g, d
Swap with a partner and read their words
exit: Write the word kid.
Read this caption: A cat.
lessons.homework: Read the words cat, dog, kid at home to a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: reduce picture choices and use letter cards. EAL: act out each word. Stretch: write two sentences.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Letters g o c k and tricky words
lessons.title: Tricky words: I, the, to, no, go
objectives: Read tricky words I, the, to, no, go
Use tricky words in simple sentences

keywords.def: a word that has a letter or sound that does not follow the rules we know yet
words that make sense together, with a capital letter and a full stop

starter: Read: cat, dog, kid, cot
Sound talk: g-o
Say bismillah and tell me a word that starts with sss.

teach.heading: What is a tricky word?
bullets: We cannot sound out every letter
teach.note: Explain gently: we sound out most words, but a few words have letters that act differently. We learn those in a special way. Do not make children anxious about them.

teach.heading: I, no, go
teach.note: Show each word. For ‘no’ and ‘go’ note that the o says its name /oh/ - the tricky part. Children sound out n-o, g-o and say ‘o says oh’. Highlight the tricky part with a heart or coloured dot.

teach.heading: the, to
teach.note: ‘the’ and ‘to’ are tricky: the letter e in ‘the’ sounds like a short /uh/ and ‘to’ is /too/. Say the word, show it, say it again. Repeat several times with fast flash-card practice.

teach.heading: Words in a sentence
teach.note: Read a short sentence together using tricky words and known sounds: ‘I go to the dog.’ Point to each word as you read. Encourage children to read tricky words by sight.

practice: Show me the tricky words I, the, to, no, go
Read each word quickly when I show the card
Read a sentence with a partner: ‘I go to the cat.’
Match tricky word cards to their pictures in the sentences
independent: Practise reading five tricky word cards three times each
Use ‘I go to the…’ to make your own sentence and say it aloud
exit: Read these words: the, no, go
Which word says /too/?
lessons.homework: Read the five tricky words to someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND: use smaller group of words and a matching game. EAL: use gesture for ‘go’ and ‘no’. Stretch: write ‘I go to the…’.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Letters g o c k and tricky words
lessons.title: Reading a simple sentence
objectives: Read a sentence containing known sounds and tricky words
Understand that a sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop

keywords.def: a group of words that makes sense
a dot that shows the end of a sentence

starter: Read: I, the, to, no, go
Read: cat, dog, tin, pig
What does a full stop look like?

teach.heading: Look at the sentence
teach.note: Display the sentence. Point to the capital T and full stop. Ask: ‘How many words?’ Count three. Read it twice: first slowly by blending, then smoothly.

teach.heading: Read it again
teach.note: Reading fluency: blend the first time, read for meaning the second. Encourage children to track with their finger. Reread to build fluency.

teach.heading: Read more sentences
teach.note: Read each sentence together. Point out any tricky words (I, the, to, no, go). Ask a question about each: ‘What sat?’ to develop comprehension.

teach.heading: Write a sentence
bullets: Write it with capital and full stop
teach.note: Model: say ‘The dog sat.’ Hold up three fingers. Write each word. Reread. Children write their own using a picture as a stimulus.

practice: Read the sentence: The cat sat.
Point to the capital letter and the full stop
Read together: A pig sat. I go to the dog.
Answer: What sat? Who goes to the dog?
independent: Write one sentence about the picture on your sheet
Check: capital, spaces, full stop
exit: Read: The dog sat.
Where is the full stop?
lessons.homework: Read a short sentence to a family member and show them the full stop.
lessons.send: SEND: sentence strips and word cards. EAL: teach ‘sentence’ with pictures. Stretch: write two sentences.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Letters ck e u r, captions and stories
lessons.title: Letters ck and e
objectives: Say the sounds ck and e
Read words: neck, deck, pen, hen

keywords.def: two letters that make one sound /k/ at the end of a word
the sound at the start of egg

starter: Read: The cat sat.
Say the sounds: c k g o s a t p
Blend: p-e-t

teach.heading: The sound e
teach.note: The short e as in egg and elephant. Not ‘ee’. Show elephant picture. Children say the sound and open their mouth slightly.

teach.heading: Writing e
teach.note: Model: draw the line across, then round and up. Children write on whiteboards. Remind them: not a backwards 3.

teach.heading: ck says /k/
bullets: At the end of a word: duck
teach.note: Teach: ck is a digraph - two letters, one sound. Usually at the end of short words after a short vowel. Show duck, sock, neck. Children say /k/ and tap once.

teach.heading: Read ck words
teach.note: Sound-talk: n-e-ck (3 sounds). Children push fingers for each sound: n, e, ck. Contrast with cat (c-a-t). Practise reading each word.

practice: Read the words: pen, hen, ten, net
Say the sounds /k/ for c, k and ck
Sound-talk and read: neck, sock, duck
Write the word ‘duck’ with one finger per sound (d-u-ck)
independent: Write ck words on whiteboards: sock, neck
Draw a duck and write a caption: A duck.
exit: Which sound do c, k and ck all make?
Read the word neck.
lessons.homework: Look for words with ck at home and read them.
lessons.send: SEND: use coloured pens for ck. EAL: practise saying /k/ clearly. Stretch: write a sentence: A duck on a deck.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Letters ck e u r, captions and stories
lessons.title: Letters u and r
objectives: Say and write the sounds u and r
Read words: run, rug, up, red

keywords.def: the sound at the start of up
the sound at the start of rat

starter: Read: sock, neck, pen, hen
Say the sounds: e ck c k o g
Blend: r-u-n

teach.heading: The sound u
teach.note: Short u as in umbrella and up. Not the letter name ‘you’. Children say the sound and stretch it.

teach.heading: Writing u
teach.note: Model: down, curve at the bottom, up, then straight down. Many children forget the last stroke and write a ‘v’ shape.

teach.heading: The sound r
teach.note: Say ‘rrr’ like a lion growling. Not ‘ruh’. Pictures: rat, rug, rain.

teach.heading: Writing r
teach.note: Model: line down, retrace up, small hook. Compare with n: r has a short arm only. Check on camera.

practice: Say the sounds: u r e ck
Read: run, rug, up
Sound-talk and blend: r-u-g, r-e-d, r-a-t
Real or alien? rud, run, rup
independent: Write r and u in a line, then write rug
Match words to pictures: run, rug, red, rat
exit: What sound does u make? What sound does r make?
Read rug.
lessons.homework: Look for r and u in your name or around your home.
lessons.send: SEND: use a rug picture with tactile letters. EAL: practise r with a growling lion. Stretch: write ‘A red rug.’

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Letters ck e u r, captions and stories
lessons.title: Reading words and sentences with all our sounds
objectives: Read words with s a t p i n m d g o c k ck e u r
Read short sentences fluently

keywords.def: reading smoothly without stopping at every word

starter: Say all the sounds in the set quickly
Read the tricky words: I, the, to, no, go
Segment: duck - how many sounds?

teach.heading: Sound button review
bullets: Put a dot under each sound
teach.note: Show the word ‘duck’ with dots under d and u, and a bar under ck. Children say the sounds and blend. Revisit sound buttons for 3-4 words.

teach.heading: Word list
teach.note: Display each word and let children blend, then say the word. Keep a quick pace. Mix in tricky words.

teach.heading: Short sentences
teach.note: Show each sentence; children read it twice: blending first, then smoothly. Check ‘can’ is decodable: c-a-n. Ask comprehension questions.

teach.heading: Check understanding
teach.note: Ask quick questions after each sentence to check children are reading for meaning. Accept short answers and model full sentences.

practice: Read: mud, rug, sock, hen
Read: I, the, to, no, go
Put your finger on the full stop
Read the three sentences with a partner
Answer: Who can run?
independent: Read a mini book page with 2-3 sentences
Draw your favourite page and write a caption
exit: Read: I got a red hat.
Who is the sentence about?
lessons.homework: Read a sentence to someone at home and talk about it.
lessons.send: SEND: read a shorter sentence and use sound buttons. EAL: label sentence items with images. Stretch: write your own sentence.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Letters ck e u r, captions and stories
lessons.title: Writing captions and a short sentence
objectives: Write a caption using sounds we know
Write a short sentence with a capital letter and full stop

keywords.def: a few words that tell about a picture
words that make sense, starting with a capital letter

starter: Say the sounds quickly
Read: A red rug.
Segment: neck - how many sounds?

teach.heading: Look at a picture
teach.note: Show a picture (a duck on a rug). Ask ‘What can you see?’ and encourage full sentence answers: ‘I can see a duck.’ Model.

teach.heading: Say it, count it, write it
bullets: Hold up your fingers for each word
Write a letter for each sound
teach.note: Teach the habit: say it, count the words on fingers, then write. This keeps sentences in memory. Model ‘A duck sat.’ on the board.

teach.heading: Write
teach.note: Remind of the three checks. Model a finger space between words. Children write their own sentence.

teach.heading: Check it
teach.note: Children point and read their sentence back. Tell them to fix one thing if needed. Praise each success; share two examples on camera.

practice: Read: I can run.
Show me a finger space
Write a caption for the picture: A pig
Write the sentence ‘A duck sat.’
independent: Write your own sentence about a picture
Check with your partner: capital, spaces, full stop
exit: Write: The dog ran.
What do we put at the end?
lessons.homework: Draw a picture and write a sentence about it using sounds you know.
lessons.send: SEND: use sentence strips; scribe if needed. EAL: use picture word mats. Stretch: add a describing word: red, big.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Letters ck e u r, captions and stories
lessons.title: Story time: retelling and our favourite sounds
objectives: Listen to and retell a simple story
Recap all sounds learned and celebrate our reading

keywords.def: words that tell about people or animals and what happens
tell a story again in your own words

starter: Say bismillah and say the sounds we know
Read: red, sock, duck, run
Which tricky words can you read?

teach.heading: Listen to a story
teach.note: Tell the traditional story of the Gingerbread Man with actions. The man baked by an old woman runs away, escapes several animals, and a fox tricks him on the river. Ask children to join in with ‘Run, run, as fast as you can’.

teach.heading: Story order
teach.note: Show three picture cards: baking, running, fox. Children put them in order and say what happens. Introduces story structure.

teach.heading: Retell it
teach.note: Model a retelling with words like first, then, at the end. Ask children to retell in pairs, using pictures if needed. Encourage full sentences.

teach.heading: Celebrate our sounds
teach.note: Celebrate the month’s progress with a quick sound quiz, a ‘show me your best letter’ and a reading success moment. Say alhamdulillah for what we have learned.

practice: Read: duck, sock, run, hen
Say what a full stop does
Put the story pictures in order and tell it with ‘first, then, at the end’
Answer: Who ran away? What did the fox do?
independent: Draw your favourite part of the story and write a caption
Retell the story to a partner using three words: first, then, end
exit: What happens at the start of the story?
Read this word: run.
lessons.homework: Retell the Gingerbread Man to a family member.
lessons.send: SEND: use story props and pictures. EAL: encourage retelling in home language and English. Stretch: write one sentence about the story.
